::: {#thm-traversal-length}
#### A traversal has one entry for each vertex

For every binary tree $T$ (@def-binary-tree),

$$
\operatorname{len}\paren{\operatorname{preorder}(T)} = \operatorname{len}\paren{\operatorname{inorder}(T)} = \operatorname{len}\paren{\operatorname{postorder}(T)} = \operatorname{size}(T),
$$

where $\operatorname{len}$ is the length of a list (@def-list-length) and $\operatorname{size}(T)$ is the number of vertices (@rem-size-height).

:::

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: proof

We use structural induction (@def-structural-induction) on $T$.

**Base case.**
All three traversals of $\mathtt{nil}$ are $\mathtt{empty}$, of length $0 = \operatorname{size}(\mathtt{nil})$.

**Inductive step.**
Let $T = \operatorname{node}(x, L, R)$, where the three lengths for $L$ are $\operatorname{size}(L)$ and those for $R$ are $\operatorname{size}(R)$.
By @thm-append-length and the definition of $\operatorname{len}$, for the preorder (@def-preorder),

$$
\ba
& \operatorname{len}\paren{\operatorname{preorder}(T)}
\\&= 1 + \operatorname{len}\paren{\operatorname{app}\paren{\operatorname{preorder}(L), \operatorname{preorder}(R)}}
\\&= 1 + \operatorname{len}\paren{\operatorname{preorder}(L)} + \operatorname{len}\paren{\operatorname{preorder}(R)}
\\&= 1 + \operatorname{size}(L) + \operatorname{size}(R),
\ea
$$

for the inorder (@def-inorder),

$$
\ba
& \operatorname{len}\paren{\operatorname{inorder}(T)}
\\&= \operatorname{len}\paren{\operatorname{inorder}(L)} + \operatorname{len}\paren{\operatorname{cons}\paren{x, \operatorname{inorder}(R)}}
\\&= \operatorname{len}\paren{\operatorname{inorder}(L)} + 1 + \operatorname{len}\paren{\operatorname{inorder}(R)}
\\&= \operatorname{size}(L) + 1 + \operatorname{size}(R),
\ea
$$

and for the postorder (@def-postorder),

$$
\ba
& \operatorname{len}\paren{\operatorname{postorder}(T)}
\\&= \operatorname{len}\paren{\operatorname{postorder}(L)} + \operatorname{len}\paren{\operatorname{app}\paren{\operatorname{postorder}(R), \operatorname{cons}(x, \mathtt{empty})}}
\\&= \operatorname{len}\paren{\operatorname{postorder}(L)} + \operatorname{len}\paren{\operatorname{postorder}(R)} + \operatorname{len}\paren{\operatorname{cons}(x, \mathtt{empty})}
\\&= \operatorname{size}(L) + \operatorname{size}(R) + 1.
\ea
$$

Each of these is $\operatorname{size}(T)$, by @rem-size-height.
By structural induction, the equations hold for every binary tree.

:::

:::
